thag3.14:1.2: While in the early texts we normally find _pettivisaya_ (“domain of the forefathers”), the idea of the _peta_ (“departed”) came to predominate in Buddhist usage, taking on the connotation of the “hungry ghost”. Normally _peta_ in early texts just means someone who has departed, regardless of what realm they end up in ([an10.177]()). Rarely, we find the idea of the departed as a distinct one of the five or six realms ([thag19.1:38.4](), [thig16.1:28.3]()), but this is the only occurrence of _petaloka_ (“world of the departed”).
thag3.14:3.1: _Sambhava_ means “creation, production”. The text is bridging the gap between _bhava_ as the “states of existence” referred to above, and the “creation’ of those states, i.e. craving, referred to below.
